speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I need to assess this newborn presenting with respiratory distress. Can you tell me the gestational age at birth and if there were any complications during delivery?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Doctor
text: Was the amniotic fluid clear, or did it appear meconium-stained? I also need to know if the baby has developed any signs of infection, such as fever or lethargy.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Tachypnea, Subcostal and intercostal retractions, Nasal flaring, Cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the maternal diabetes and prematurity, I am concerned about transient tachypnea of the newborn or respiratory distress syndrome. REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Ground-glass appearance, air bronchograms, suggesting Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)

speaker: Doctor
text: The chest X-ray findings of ground-glass appearance and air bronchograms, combined with the history of prematurity and maternal diabetes, strongly support a diagnosis of Respiratory Distress Syndrome. DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)
